why: Every dataset records its source, licence, checksum and shape, and synthetic data has to declare itself.
Downloads once, checksums the bytes, and makes reruns reproducible offline.
Training fills the report as it runs, so the write-up cannot drift from what happened.

skill: Runtime leakage assertions with a ledger
why: Each check records what it measured; deleting a check deletes its evidence.
Flags fitting on held-out data, shuffled time splits and unseeded estimators.
Guarantees training ends before testing starts, with a gap against boundary bleed.
Papers, abstracts and result tables are regenerated from artifacts; CI fails if they drift.
Screenshots are only saved as evidence after the view is confirmed to show its expected content.
Meter distance, fare and arrival time are unknowable at booking, so the model may not use them.

skill: Data cleaning with an audit trail
why: Each filter records how many rows it removed and why.
Missing fields cluster by vendor, so the gap itself is kept as a feature.
No row contributes to its own encoding, and rare categories shrink toward the mean.
23:00 and 00:00 end up as neighbours rather than opposite ends of a scale.
Ramer-Douglas-Peucker turns the official shapefile into a small SVG map.
Average precision and review-budget recall replace accuracy, which a do-nothing model maximises.
Reports how much fraud a fixed-size analyst team would actually catch.
Detectors that never see labels are scored against labels, alongside supervised models.

skill: Serving the model that actually won
why: The API loads the tournament winner rather than a hardcoded estimator.
Price levels give a near-perfect R² for free; returns remove the illusion.
Features are recomputed on truncated history and must match, proving they never read the future.
The Parkinson estimator uses the day's high and low, not just closes.
Scores a whole predictive distribution rather than a single point.
Repeated out-of-sample refits, dropping training rows whose targets overlap the test block.
Asks whether a winner beats a random walk or just got lucky.
A strategy is always compared with simply holding, net of execution cost.
Student-t quantiles over EWMA volatility, because returns have heavy tails.
One loader for two projects, recording what each rule removed, including a nine-day overlap between source sheets.
Segments are built from one year and scored on the next, so they have to predict something they never saw.
Corrects variance explained for the number of segments, so more clusters are not rewarded by default.
Rebuilds each segmentation on overlapping subsamples and compares assignments with the adjusted Rand index.
The classic marketing heuristic every learned segmentation has to beat.
Hides one product from each later basket so every method, rules included, is judged on the same task.
Frequent itemsets mined after pruning items below support, turned into single-consequent rules.
A sparse co-occurrence matrix as a threshold-free baseline, which won the tournament.
Recomputes every mined rule on later baskets to see whether its association still holds.

skill: Custom checks in the audit trail
why: Project-specific leakage rules recorded in the same ledger as the standard assertions.
Explicit ordering so results do not change with Python's randomised string hashing.

skill: Minimum lag equal to the forecast horizon
why: Every feature must exist when a day-ahead forecast is issued; enforced by an assertion in training.

skill: Measuring the cost of a leak
why: Scores a deliberately leaky model the same way and reports how much it would have flattered the result.
Hours with too few readings stay missing and are excluded from training and scoring.
Checks whether an 80% band actually contains 80% of outcomes, shared by both forecasting projects.
Plants known leaks in copies of a real script so the auditor can be measured rather than trusted.

skill: Balanced accuracy for a skewed benchmark
why: Stops a detector that flags everything from looking good on a corpus with more leaks than controls.
Runs each variant with assertions off to see how much its leak changes the published number.

skill: Population stability index for drift monitoring
why: Bins a column on the reference data's quantiles and compares shares, with a floor so empty bins do not divide by zero.

skill: Evaluating a retraining policy on unseen months
why: Lets each policy choose training months from those already finished, then scores it on the next month, as a deployed model would be.
Retrains only when the latest finished month drifts past the PSI threshold, so the alarm's value can be measured against simpler policies.

skill: Load testing a FastAPI model server
why: Starts the real API, warms it up and records throughput and latency percentiles at several concurrency levels.
Uses LightGBM's pred_contrib so every served estimate comes with contributions that sum exactly to it.

skill: Group fairness metrics at a threshold
why: Reports disparate impact, equal-opportunity and false-positive gaps and selection rates, so accuracy is never read alone.
Trains each model with and without sensitive attributes and asserts the unaware version truly excludes them.
Approximate nearest-neighbour search whose recall and scanned fraction are measured against exact search.

skill: Quiz answers checked on the server
why: Questions are served without answers, and explanations quote figures from the training run.
Greedy forward selection with replacement over out-of-fold predictions, with deterministic tie-breaking and a recorded trajectory.
Gives every training row a prediction from a model that never saw it, and averages the fold models for the test set.

skill: Paired bootstrap of an AUC difference
why: Resamples the same test rows for both models, so a verdict reflects the models and not which rows were drawn.

skill: Running a conflicting library in its own environment
why: AutoGluon hands over test probabilities as a file, checked against the shared test set, instead of changing the shared environment.
Recovers a year the file does not store, so a chronological split is possible.

skill: Naive Bayes written out and matched to a library
why: Every word's evidence is visible, and training asserts its probabilities equal scikit-learn's.

skill: Largest stable learning rate for least squares
why: Computes 2 / largest eigenvalue, the limit beyond which batch gradient descent diverges.
Verifies every hand-derived gradient without trusting any framework.

skill: Measuring a duplicate leak across many splits
why: Compares scores with and without deduplication over twenty seeds, so a small effect is not mistaken for noise or vice versa.

skill: Kahn's algorithm with a concrete cycle
why: Linear-time ordering that, on failure, returns one closed path instead of just 'cycle detected'.
Counts open, usable and dead inputs per node so scheduling is O((V + E) log V), with retries, branches and join modes.

skill: Differential testing against a slow reference
why: Keeps the simple implementation as an oracle; it found a real double-start bug in the optimised one.
Plants realistic bugs in copies of the code and requires the tests to fail on every one.
Branded ids and exhaustive switches are tested: a type change that lets a bad line compile fails the build.
An edit names the version it was based on; a stale edit is refused with the current task instead of overwriting it.
Every event carries a global sequence number, so a tab that misses one reloads instead of drifting out of sync.
Resolves relative dates against an explicit day and keeps any marker it cannot parse in the title.

skill: Generated round-trip tests for a parser
why: Renders known fields into text in random order and requires every one to come back, independently of hand-written cases.
Runs the real server with many subscribers and checks completeness, order and latency of every event.

skill: Masking label words to measure a text leak
why: Removes every word of any class name, so a text model's score without the answer written in the input can be measured.

skill: Grouped split by a shared key
why: Keeps products sharing a display name on one side, checked by an executed assertion across train, validation and test.

skill: Cached CLIP image and text embeddings
why: Embeds 44,000 images and names once on the GPU and reuses them while the product ids match.
Weighted geometric mean of per-modality probabilities, with weights searched on validation products only.
Ranks product photos by similarity to a typed description, served live.
Runs both versions on the same seed so split-to-split variation cancels, then bootstraps the differences.
Encodes each training row from the other folds, so a row's own label never enters its own feature.
Handles both quoting conventions OpenML serves, so a comma inside a quoted value cannot split a row.

skill: A claim that must match its interval
why: An executed assertion refuses to publish an effect whose bootstrap interval covers zero.
